title: Counting triples with a fixed index and coordinate vector
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$, an index $i \in \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, and a function $\mathrm{coords}$ assigning to each index in $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ one of the three disjointness labels *neither*, *leftOnly*, or *rightOnly*. Then there are exactly three triples $(a, f, c)$, where $a$ is an index, $f$ is such a labelling function, and $c$ is a single disjointness label, subject to the constraints $a = i$ and $f = \mathrm{coords}$.
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number
i is an index in Fin n
coords is a function from Fin n to the three-element disjointness-label type
the triple's first component equals i
the triple's second (function) component equals coords
